summary: BYD's folding steering wheel sparks trending buzz, Fangchengbao Titan 9 launch hits the high-end market, XPeng posts record Q3 revenue and deliveries, and new-energy technology pathways diversify at an accelerating pace.

articles.title: BYD unveils a foldable steering wheel, once again grabbing the spotlight through hardware innovation
articles.summary: BYD's foldable steering wheel launch has trended on Baidu, making it the most watched tech innovation in today's auto world.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Trending, BYD has officially unveiled a foldable steering wheel, with related topics quickly climbing the trending charts to become the most discussed tech event in today's automotive circle. As a Chinese NEV leader that has rolled out a stream of technologies in recent years — from the Blade Battery and e⁴ Platform to the DiSus suspension — BYD's latest move on the steering wheel, a traditional component, continues its approach of starting from underlying hardware structure to redefine the cabin and driving interaction space. Foldable steering wheels have mostly been confined to concept cars and autonomous-driving visions; BYD bringing the concept to a mass-production discussion signals that the transformation of the steering mechanism is beginning to move from concept to implementation. Industry focus centers on how a foldable steering wheel will align with levels of autonomous driving, cabin layout and safety regulations, and whether BYD will be the first to fit it in future models and disclose a specific production timeline and technical specifications. At the time of writing, BYD has yet to reveal detailed technical specs for the product or the models it will be fitted to.
articles.impact: If the foldable steering wheel reaches mass production, it would open up new possibilities for redesigning smart cabin space, drive coordinated upgrades across steering systems, seating layout and intelligent driving, and further raise the bar for technical competition among Chinese brands in chassis and human-machine interaction hardware.

articles.title: Fangchengbao Bao 9 Launches with Bookings Open, Another Step in BYD's Premium Push
articles.summary: The Fangchengbao Bao 9 launched on November 19 with bookings opened simultaneously, riding BYD's DMS hybrid system into the premium segment.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, BYD's premium brand Fangchengbao officially launched its new model, the Bao 9, on November 19, with bookings opening the same day. The company clearly stated its goal of competing in the premium market. On the same day, NetEase Auto released real-world test content focused on the vehicle's DMS hybrid system, calling it "BYD's strongest hybrid," drawing industry attention to the architecture's performance in power, energy consumption, and driving quality. Since its establishment, the Fangchengbao brand has carried BYD's mission of moving upmarket, having built recognition through its Bao series in the off-road and personalization niches. The Bao 9's launch further expands its footprint in the premium SUV segment. The official pricing range and full configuration details have not yet been released, but given the product cadence, the vehicle is expected to compete directly with premium new-energy SUVs in the same price bracket.
articles.impact: The Bao 9's launch will intensify competition in the premium new-energy SUV segment. If the DMS hybrid system earns market approval in real-world testing, it could strengthen BYD's standing in hybrid technology and lift Fangchengbao's sales mix upmarket.

articles.title: HuaJing S Five-Seat Version Debuts with Huawei Qiankun Tech and CATL Battery Cells
articles.summary: The five-seat HuaJing S debuts as standard with Huawei Qiankun technology and CATL battery cells, maxing out its intelligence and powertrain specs.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the five-seat version of the HuaJing S has officially debuted, with its biggest highlight being the level of smart features and powertrain hardware on offer: Huawei Qiankun technology and CATL battery cells come as standard. Huawei Qiankun is Huawei's advanced autonomous driving and smart cockpit solution for the intelligent vehicle sector, and has become a core selling point for many Chinese brand models. CATL cells hold industry-leading advantages in energy density, safety, and supply chain security. The launch of the five-seat version means the HuaJing S is further broadening its product lineup to cover more family-user needs. Against the backdrop of white-hot competition in the new-energy SUV market, leveraging top-tier supplier technology to quickly establish product credibility has become a common play for new brands and models. The official range, powertrain specs, and pricing for the five-seat HuaJing S have not yet been announced.
articles.impact: The standardization of top-supply-chain technology is leveling the experience gap between new brands and established players. Consumers will gain access to advanced driver assistance and mainstream powertrain configurations at a lower threshold, while forcing automakers to find differentiation in software tuning and vehicle integration.

articles.title: Yijing X9 BEV Details Emerge, Set for Launch at Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27
articles.summary: Details of the Yijing X9 battery-electric version have emerged; it will officially launch at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, becoming a pre-show focal point.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, details of the Yijing X9 battery-electric version have been revealed, with the company confirming the model will officially launch during the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27. As a key model for the Yijing brand, the X9 BEV's launch timing lands squarely on the year's largest domestic auto show, signaling the brand's intent to convert show traffic into both buzz and orders. Several automakers have recently unveiled their Guangzhou Auto Show lineups, and the Yijing X9 BEV is among the first to officially announce its launch date. Core information such as battery capacity, range, motor output, and pricing has not yet been disclosed and is expected to be revealed on launch day at the show.
articles.impact: With the Guangzhou Auto Show approaching, a dense wave of new model announcements will drive year-end buying interest. If the Yijing X9 is competitively priced, it could capture share in the battery-electric SUV market and further intensify year-end price competition.

articles.title: Real-World Test Puts Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Hybrid at Just 3.6L/100km
articles.summary: NetEase Auto's real-world test recorded fuel consumption as low as 3.6L/100km for the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale hybrid, highlighting impressive efficiency.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto's real-world test, the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale variant achieved a fuel consumption figure of 3.6L/100km, an impressive result for a compact SUV. Blue Whale is Changan's in-house powertrain brand, and Blue Whale Super Engine represents its achievements in high-efficiency hybrid technology. A tested figure of 3.6L/100km means users can significantly cut running costs in both daily commuting and long-distance travel — one of the metrics consumers are most sensitive to when making a purchase decision. The CS75 series has long ranked among the best-selling Chinese brand SUVs, and further gains in fuel efficiency will directly strengthen its value proposition against rivals in the segment.
articles.impact: The low tested fuel consumption figure provides Changan CS75 PLUS with strong marketing material, helping attract existing owners of gasoline vehicles looking to switch to more efficient models in a market sensitive to fuel prices and ownership costs.

articles.title: Tesla Says It Will Keep Raising Production in China
articles.summary: Tesla says it will continue to expand capacity in China, underscoring the market's central role in its global operations.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, Tesla has stated it will continue to increase vehicle production in China. China has become one of Tesla's largest single markets worldwide, and its Shanghai Gigafactory not only handles domestic deliveries but also serves as a key export hub. Against the backdrop of intensifying competition in the new energy vehicle market and rapidly improving products from local brands, Tesla's decision to further ramp up capacity in China reflects both a long-term bet on Chinese demand and a proactive move on cost control and supply chain efficiency. China's comprehensive NEV supply chain is a critical foundation supporting Tesla's continued expansion of local production. Tesla has not yet disclosed the scale, timeline or specific models involved in the capacity increase.
articles.impact: Tesla's capacity expansion in China will drive order growth across domestic power battery, automotive electronics and parts suppliers, while intensifying direct competition with local brands such as BYD and XPeng in mainstream price segments.

articles.title: AUDI Brand Turns Two: The Next Chapter of New Energy Has Begun
articles.summary: The AUDI brand marks its second anniversary, with officials saying the next phase of its new energy push has begun and its transformation has entered a new stage.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the AUDI brand has reached the two-year mark since its founding, reviewing and looking ahead under the theme "The Next Chapter of New Energy Has Already Begun." As a flagship camp of international luxury automakers in the electric transition, the brand has made steady progress over the past two years in expanding its product matrix, rolling out electric platforms and forging localized partnerships in the Chinese market. Officials say the brand has moved from an "investment phase" into a "deep cultivation phase," with the next stage focused on comprehensively strengthening the competitiveness of its new energy products. With BBA and other luxury brands broadly facing pressure from electrification while Chinese new energy brands accelerate their rise, how AUDI balances brand premium with the value of its electric products will be a key challenge over the next two years.
articles.impact: As luxury brands' electrification enters deep waters, AUDI's future product cadence will shape pricing and competition in the premium new energy segment, while also serving as a reference model for Sino-foreign cooperation in the new energy space.

articles.title: HEV Emerges as a Third Technical Route as More Consumers Choose Hybrids
articles.summary: Industry observers note that beyond the battery-electric versus plug-in hybrid debate, a growing number of consumers are turning to HEV hybrid models.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, outside the long-running battle between battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, HEV (hybrid electric vehicle) is quietly becoming the choice of a growing number of consumers. HEV models require no external charging, avoiding range and charging anxiety caused by underdeveloped charging infrastructure, while delivering significantly better fuel economy than conventional gasoline cars — especially friendly to users without fixed charging access. The domestic HEV market is seeing more players; Japanese brands have long held the advantage, while domestic automakers are accelerating development of hybrid-specific engines and transmissions. Globally, the hybrid route is growing across many markets, serving as an important transitional solution before full battery-electric adoption.
articles.impact: Rising HEV demand will push automakers toward more diversified powertrain strategies, with a market structure of BEV, PHEV, range-extended and HEV coexisting likely to persist long term, enabling consumers to find better-matched products for their use cases.

articles.title: XPeng Q3 Revenue and Deliveries Hit Record Highs, Q4 Deliveries Expected to Top 170,000
articles.summary: XPeng posted record quarterly revenue and deliveries in Q3, with Q4 deliveries forecast to exceed 170,000 units.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, XPeng's latest Q3 results show both revenue and deliveries hit all-time highs, with operating performance continuing to improve. More notably, XPeng's guidance points to Q4 deliveries surpassing 170,000 units. If achieved, the target would set a new single-quarter delivery record, signaling that the company's capacity ramp-up and product matrix rollout are entering a harvest phase. Against the industry backdrop, the EV startup field is clearly diverging: leading players are extending their advantages through smart-tech branding and scaled deliveries, while laggard brands face elimination pressure. XPeng's long-term investment in autonomous driving is gradually translating into tangible sales and revenue contributions, and the release of scale effects is directly significant for margin improvement.
articles.impact: XPeng's rapid delivery ramp-up will strengthen the competitive edge of leading EV startups and drive further industry consolidation, while providing a new reference point for capital markets in re-rating the profitability of new-energy vehicle players.

articles.title: Interview with Jiang Ping: Safety Should Not Be Tiered — Changan Seeks to Make Safety Tech Accessible to All
articles.summary: Changan's Jiang Ping said safety should not be split across trim levels, calling for universal access to safety technology and sparking industry debate on safety configurations.
articles.detail: In an exclusive interview with NetEase Auto, Changan Automobile's Jiang Ping said safety should not be tiered by trim level, and that Changan's goal is to make safety technology widely accessible. The remarks address a common practice in the auto industry: some automakers use active and passive safety features as differentiators between higher- and lower-spec models, leaving entry-level buyers with inferior safety. Changan advocates extending safety capabilities to products across more price points, so consumers with different budgets receive equal protection. The philosophy aligns with the shift in the new-energy vehicle industry from a price war to a value war, and echoes increasingly stringent regulatory demands on vehicle safety performance.
articles.impact: If more automakers follow the push for universal safety, it would drive standardization and wider adoption of active and passive safety features, raising the industry's baseline product safety and giving consumers access to safer vehicles at a lower threshold.

articles.title: Guangzhou Auto Show Enters Final Countdown: Year-End New Car Wave and Price War May Unfold Simultaneously
articles.summary: With models such as the Yijing X9 confirmed for a November 27 launch, the Guangzhou Auto Show's new car wave is approaching as year-end market competition heats up.
articles.detail: With the all-electric Yijing X9 confirmed for its launch at the Guangzhou Auto Show on November 27, the pace of new car debuts at this year's event has clearly accelerated. As the last major international auto show of the year, the Guangzhou Auto Show has traditionally been a key moment for automakers to push year-end sales and a bellwether for product plans in the year ahead. Combined with a dense slate of recent product moves — including the launch of the Fangchengbao Tai 9 and the debut of the Huajing S five-seat version — a wave of new energy vehicles is expected to hit the show, spanning battery-electric, plug-in hybrid, range-extended and HEV powertrains. Meanwhile, the year-end period represents automakers' final window to hit annual sales targets, and stacked price discounts and financing offers could intensify market competition further, giving consumers a richer range of choices before the year is out.
articles.impact: A concentrated wave of new car launches around the show will help release year-end purchase demand and expand consumers' bargaining room, while competition among automakers will shift from a pure price war to an all-around contest of technology, features and service.

articles.title: Technology for All Becomes the Main Theme: From Folding Steering Wheels to Accessible Safety, Chinese Automakers Enter a New Competitive Stage
articles.summary: BYD's folding steering wheel, Changan's push for universal safety and Huawei Qiankun becoming standard equipment all point to a shared industry trend of democratizing technology and upgrading the experience.
articles.detail: Taken together, today's multiple news stories show that the auto industry's competitive focus is shifting from "spec and price stacking" to "technology for all": BYD unveiled a folding steering wheel in an attempt to reshape human-machine interaction through hardware innovation; Changan's Jiang Ping publicly argued that safety should not be tiered by trim level, pushing for broader access to safety technology; and the Huajing S five-seat version makes Huawei Qiankun technology and CATL cells standard equipment, turning top-tier supply chain capabilities into features for everyone. At the same time, powertrain strategies are diversifying, with battery-electric, plug-in hybrid and HEV each finding their target audiences. Looking ahead, whoever can scale down high-value technologies at lower cost will gain the upper hand in a market defined by zero-sum competition, and consumers will be the direct beneficiaries of the technology democratization trend.
articles.impact: The diffusion of technology will accelerate industry shakeout, putting greater pressure on brands lacking core technology and cost-control capabilities, while consumers will get higher specifications, stronger performance and better safety at the same budget.
